newsitem.title: JAPAN: GDP data important for Japan budget decision--EPA.
newsitem.headline: GDP data important for Japan budget decision--EPA.

text.p: Japan's gross domestic product data for the April-June period will be looked at closely when deciding whether to draft a supplementary budget for the current fiscal year to next March, but will not be the only factor, Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Shusei Tanaka told a news conference on Thursday.
Tanaka said the April-June figure was important, but it was also necessary to look at the whole picture, to gauge the flow of the economy.
Tanaka was speaking after a meeting with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.

He quoted Hashimoto as saying there was a lot of allocated public works spending left over from the previous budget which had not been used, and which should go to help regional economies, in particular small and medium-sized companies in those economies.
Tanaka and Hashimoto also discussed the EPA's proposed deregulation plans for six key sectors, including telecommunications and distribution.
Related ministries expected to put forward concrete proposals concerning the plan by the end of the month.
Both agreed that speedy deregulation was necessary, but Hashimoto asked Tanaka to leave the date of the announcements to him.
"In order to have good results next fiscal year, we must work at a fast pace, starting now," Tanaka said.
